---

## What is ggplot2?

ggplot2 is a powerful, open-source data visualization library for R developed by **Hadley Wickham**. It is based on the **Grammar of Graphics** — a systematic framework for describing any statistical graphic as a combination of layers.

One of ggplot2's defining strengths is **layered plot construction**: start with data, map aesthetics, add geometric objects, then refine with scales, facets, and themes — each `+` call adds a new layer.

```r
install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)
```

---

## Basic Template

```r
ggplot(data = <DATA>, mapping = aes(<MAPPINGS>)) +
  <GEOM_FUNCTION>(
    mapping  = aes(<MAPPINGS>),
    stat     = <STAT>,
    position = <POSITION>
  ) +
  <COORDINATE_FUNCTION> +
  <FACET_FUNCTION> +
  <SCALE_FUNCTION> +
  <THEME_FUNCTION>
```

Minimal working example:

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point()
```

---

## The 7 Layers of Grammar of Graphics

| Layer | Purpose | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| **1. Data** | The data frame to visualize | `ggplot(data = mtcars)` |
| **2. Aesthetics** | Map variables to visual properties | `aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))` |
| **3. Geometries** | Shape used to represent data | `geom_point()`, `geom_line()`, `geom_bar()` |
| **4. Facets** | Split into sub-panels | `facet_wrap(~ cyl)` |
| **5. Statistics** | Statistical transformation | `stat_smooth()`, `stat_bin()` |
| **6. Coordinates** | Coordinate system | `coord_flip()`, `coord_polar()` |
| **7. Themes** | Non-data visual appearance | `theme_minimal()`, `theme(...)` |

---

## Aesthetics (aes)

The `aes()` function maps data variables to visual properties. There are two kinds:

- **Mapped** (inside `aes()`) — value varies by data
- **Fixed** (outside `aes()`) — constant for all data points

```r
# MAPPED — colour changes per group
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point()

# FIXED — all points are steelblue, size 3
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 3, alpha = 0.7)

# BOTH — shape mapped to data, colour fixed
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt, shape = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(colour = "tomato", size = 3)
```

### Aesthetic reference

| Aesthetic | Maps to | Example |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `x` | Horizontal axis position | `aes(x = weight)` |
| `y` | Vertical axis position | `aes(y = height)` |
| `colour` | Outline / point colour | `aes(colour = species)` |
| `fill` | Fill colour (bars, areas) | `aes(fill = group)` |
| `size` | Point size / line width | `aes(size = population)` |
| `shape` | Point shape (0–24) | `aes(shape = type)` |
| `alpha` | Transparency (0–1) | `aes(alpha = confidence)` |
| `linetype` | Solid / dashed / dotted | `aes(linetype = group)` |
| `label` | Text labels | `aes(label = name)` |
| `group` | Grouping without visual encoding | `aes(group = id)` |

---

## Building a Plot Step by Step

```r
library(ggplot2)

# Step 1: data + aesthetics
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg))

# Step 2: add geometry
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point()

# Step 3: map colour to a third variable
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3)

# Step 4: add a smooth trend line
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

# Step 5: labels
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Weight vs MPG", colour = "Cylinders",
       x = "Weight (1,000 lbs)", y = "Miles per Gallon")

# Step 6: theme
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Weight vs MPG", colour = "Cylinders",
       x = "Weight (1,000 lbs)", y = "Miles per Gallon") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## Scales

Scales control how data values map to visual properties.

```r
# Axis limits
scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 50), breaks = seq(0, 50, by = 10))
scale_y_log10()
scale_x_date(date_labels = "%Y-%m")
scale_x_reverse()

# Colour & fill — continuous
scale_colour_gradient(low = "white", high = "darkred")
scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0)

# Colour & fill — discrete
scale_colour_manual(values = c("#e84855", "#2d6be4", "#12a36a"))
scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")
scale_colour_viridis_d()          # colorblind-friendly

# Axis labels
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format())
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)
scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar)
```

---

## Faceting

Faceting splits data into multiple sub-panels.

```r
library(ggplot2)

# facet_wrap — one variable
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ gear)

# Custom rows / columns
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ cyl, nrow = 1)

# Free scales per panel
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ cyl, scales = "free")

# facet_grid — two variables
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(am ~ cyl)            # rows ~ columns

# Only column facets
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(. ~ cyl)
```

---

## Key ggplot2 Functions

```r
# Labels
labs(title = , subtitle = , caption = , x = , y = , colour = , fill = , tag = )
ggtitle("Title", subtitle = "Subtitle")
xlab("X axis")  ;  ylab("Y axis")

# Coordinates
coord_flip()                    # swap x and y
coord_polar(theta = "y")        # pie / radar charts
coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0,5))  # zoom without dropping data
coord_fixed()                   # equal unit lengths on both axes

# Annotations
annotate("text",  x = 2, y = 3, label = "Note")
annotate("rect",  xmin = 1, xmax = 2, ymin = 0, ymax = 5, alpha = 0.1)
annotate("segment", x = 1, y = 1, xend = 3, yend = 3, arrow = arrow())

# Theme shortcuts
theme_grey()       # default
theme_bw()         # black & white
theme_minimal()    # no background
theme_classic()    # axes only, no grid
theme_dark()       # dark panel
theme_void()       # blank canvas

# Set global theme
old <- theme_set(theme_minimal())
theme_set(old)     # restore

# Save
ggsave("plot.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

---

## The theme() Function

The `theme()` function overrides any non-data visual element:

```r
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(
    # Text elements
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 12, colour = "grey50"),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 1),
    axis.title        = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text         = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x       = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),

    # Panel
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "#f0f4f8"),
    panel.grid.major  = element_line(colour = "#dce3ec", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    panel.border      = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA),

    # Legend
    legend.position   = "top",
    legend.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),

    # Margins
    plot.margin       = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20)
  )
```

### theme() element functions

| Function | Used for |
|----------|----------|
| `element_text(face, size, colour, hjust, vjust, angle)` | Text elements |
| `element_line(colour, linewidth, linetype)` | Lines & grid |
| `element_rect(fill, colour, linewidth)` | Backgrounds & borders |
| `element_blank()` | Remove an element |

---

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip — save & store your theme

Create a custom theme object once and reuse it across all your plots:

```r
my_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  )

# Apply to any plot
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  my_theme
```
:::
